title: Continuous Latent Diffusion Language Model
note: Reference 1. Primary source — architecture, four research questions, baseline-matching conditions, latent-dimension/noise-level tables, §5.1 perplexity case, Appendix 12.4 limitations, §5.5 image experiment, §6 conclusion. 11 authors. v1, 2026-05-07, 99 pages, CC BY 4.0.

title: Cola DLM Project Page
note: Reference 2. Source for the authors' own §2.2 summary of benchmark advantages (MMLU, RACE, Story Cloze, OBQA) and scaling-curve claim at ~2000 EFLOPs. A prose summary, not a printed per-benchmark table.

title: First-author blog post on Cola DLM
note: Reference 3. Source for §1.2 (continuity alone carries no theoretical guarantee over discreteness; the motivation was representation, not diffusion), §2.1 compute constraints, §3.1 conservative settings.

title: ByteDance-Seed/Cola-DLM (GitHub repository README)
note: Reference 4. Source for the §2.3 table's left column (eight benchmarks, average 26.65), the repository's own note that this average runs slightly higher than the paper's final average, §4.3 text-only release scope, §2.4 run-example defaults. Apache 2.0, repository created 2026-05-15.

title: ByteDance-Seed/Cola-DLM (Hugging Face model card)
note: Reference 5. Source for the §2.3 table's right column (RACE 19.60, SIQA 28.90, average 26.75) with its own 'zero-shot' label, the claim that the released weights sit at the largest-budget point on the scaling curve, tokenizer vocabulary size 100,278, and the usage restrictions quoted in the reinforced §2.3 passage.

title: NeurIPS 2026 poster session page (#S4308)
note: Reference 6. Source for the poster slot (8 December 2026, 10:00-13:00 AEDT, Hall 1-4, #S4308). The page does not state whether this is a main-conference or workshop track.

title: Cola2: ... Balanced Discrete Generation
note: Reference 7. Source for the §5.2 masked-diffusion-decoder description and the two experiment figures taken from the abstract. This abstract does not name Cola DLM. v1, 2026-10-22.

title: Diffusion-LM Improves Controllable Text Generation
note: Reference 8. §5.1 precedent — ran continuous diffusion directly on word vectors.

title: Latent Diffusion for Language Generation
note: Reference 9. §5.1 precedent — ran diffusion over the latent space of an already-trained encoder-decoder.

title: TextLDM: Language Modeling with Continuous Latent Diffusion
note: Reference 10. Source for the §3.4 quotation (reconstruction fidelity alone is insufficient) and the §5.1 same-month independent design point. A separate team of 13 authors.

title: Large Language Diffusion Models
note: Reference 11. LLaDA — primary source for discrete masked diffusion over tokens and this paper's baseline.

title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
note: Reference 12. §1.1 primary source for flow matching.

title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
note: Reference 13. DiT — primary source for the diffusion transformer, grounding the §1.2 claim that the transformer architecture stays in place.

title: 2 OLMo 2 Furious
note: Reference 14. §2 primary source for the tokenizer shared by all three models.

title: DiffusionGemma: The Diffusion Model That Writes a Sentence All at Once
note: Reference 15. Pebblous's own June article on a token-space diffusion language model, used in §1 and §5 as the dividing line between the two branches (token-space vs. continuous-latent diffusion).

title: Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality: How Diffusion Models Efficiently Learn Low-Dimensional Distributions
note: Reference 16. Pebblous article on the premise that data live on a low-dimensional structure, touching the Appendix 12.4 assumption.

title: VQ-Tokenizer: The Technical Backbone of Data Quality and Synthetic Data
note: Reference 17. Cited for the point that the unit a dataset is cut into changes what a model sees.
